fields.meta_description: A web hosting landing page sells a plan to someone comparing hosts. See four examples and build one that saves every Order click.
fields.h1: Build a Web Hosting Landing Page That Sells Plans
fields.hero_description: Build a web hosting landing page with plan cards, the renewal price in view, and every Order click saved to a database you own.
fields.explore_cta: Build My Web Hosting Landing Page
fields.features_heading: The Parts of a Page That Sells Hosting
fields.features_subheading: Buyers open several hosts side by side before they pick one. Six parts of the page decide whether the Order click lands on yours.
fields.feature_1:
Plan cards that show the renewal price

Emergent builds a card for each plan with the intro price, the term it covers, and the renewal price set in smaller type beneath. A buyer sees the second-year cost before checkout.
fields.feature_2:
One toggle for monthly and yearly prices

A toggle above the cards switches every plan between its monthly price and its 12-month price. Change a price once by prompt, and the app updates that card in both views at once.
fields.feature_3:
Order clicks saved by plan and term

Every Order button saves a row to a database you own, with the plan and billing term, stamped with the time of the click. Sort the rows by week to see which plan sells best.
fields.feature_4:
A migration form with alerts

Switchers name their current host, site address, and size. The app sends each request by email or Slack to the people you pick, and you set which sizes go to an engineer first.
fields.feature_5:
Orders handed to your billing system

Connect the billing or control panel tool you already run through its API. The app passes the chosen plan and term along with each order and pulls current prices back into the cards.
fields.feature_6:
A page you can take with you

Export the page to your GitHub repository on paid plans and run it on your own servers. Or keep it on Emergent under your own domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits.

fields.tab_content_1:
Each Order click, saved with its plan and term

Saltmarch Hosting sells three shared plans. Each card prints the 12-month price, with the renewal price under it in smaller type. Each click on an Order button is stored with the plan and the term. In October the page logged 1,240 Order clicks. Business drew 588 of them and Starter 412, while Pro took the other 240.
fields.tab_content_2:
Any site over 10 GB goes to Juniper

Ferriby Web moves sites for free. Its request form asks for the current host, the site address, and the site size. Any site over 10 GB posts to the #migrations Slack channel and tags Juniper Lantz, who plans large moves. This week brought 37 requests, and 9 of them were over 10 GB.
fields.tab_content_3:
Scale for any site over 50,000 monthly visits

Tamberline Hosting's WordPress page asks for monthly visits and the number of sites. Any site over 50,000 monthly visits gets the Scale plan. Below that, single-site owners get Starter, and multi-site owners get Studio. Each answer is saved with the plan the page showed.
fields.tab_content_4:
After 14 days, 520 names on the Toronto list

Hollowfen Cloud is opening a Toronto region for its VPS plans, and the waitlist page asks for an email and a server size. Each signup is saved with the size picked. In the first 14 days, 520 people joined. The 2 vCPU size led with 311 signups, which tells Hollowfen which servers to stock first.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Web Hosting Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a web hosting landing page with clear prices and a saved record of every order, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the plans the page sells
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Show the renewal price on the card
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Promise only what you can back
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Give switchers a way to move
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose two to four plans and mark the one you expect to sell best. A page that lists the whole catalog leaves the visitor to do the comparing. Link the rest of the lineup from one line under the cards.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Put the price after the first term on the card itself, in smaller type below the intro price, and name the term it applies to. A buyer should never meet the higher number for the first time at checkout.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Any figure the page gives for reliability or speed should use the exact number and wording of your service agreement, with a link to it. If the agreement states no figure, leave it off and show the regions you run.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Visitors who host elsewhere want to know how their site gets to you. Add a short request form for the current host, the address, and the size, and decide which sizes an engineer handles in person.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Describe the page in one prompt
fields.howto_step_5_des: Name each plan with its intro and renewal prices, and list the forms you want on the page. Emergent builds the cards and the database the Order clicks land in. Change any card later with another prompt.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Connect orders to your billing system
fields.howto_step_6_des: Link the Order buttons to your billing software through its API. Each Order click then carries the chosen plan into checkout. Until that connection is live, point the buttons at the signup page you use today.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test every Order button before launch
fields.howto_step_7_des: Click Order on each plan from a phone and a laptop, then send a test migration request above your size limit. Check that every row lands with the right plan and term before you publish on your own domain (built into Emergent, uses credits).

faq_plan.q: What is a web hosting landing page?
faq_plan.a: A web hosting landing page is the page a hosting company sends ad and search traffic to, built to sell one plan or a small set of them. It shows each plan's price and term, what the plan includes, and an Order button that starts checkout.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a web hosting landing page?
faq_plan.a: Describe your plans and their prices in a prompt to Emergent's AI landing page builder. It builds the page and a database for the Order clicks. Connect your billing software next, and test an order on each plan before the page goes live.

faq_plan.q: Where can I host a landing page for free?
faq_plan.ref: Where can I host a landing page for free?

prov.original: Where can I host a landing page for free?

faq_plan.a: On the free tier of a page builder. Emergent's free tier covers building and publishing. When the page needs your own address, custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits.

faq_plan.q: What should a hosting landing page include?
faq_plan.a: A hosting landing page needs one card per plan with the intro and renewal prices side by side, plus the limits buyers compare, such as storage and email accounts. Add an Order button to every card and a short form for visitors who want to move a site from another host.

faq_plan.q: Should a web hosting landing page show the renewal price?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Print it on the plan card, right under the intro price, and say how long the intro price lasts. Buyers compare hosts on the second-year cost too, and a renewal price they find for the first time on an invoice turns into a support ticket.

faq_plan.q: How many plans should a web hosting landing page compare?
faq_plan.a: Two to four. Choose the highlighted plan from data: count Order clicks for each plan over a month, and move the highlight if buyers keep picking a different card. Plans past the fourth belong on a separate pricing page.

faq_plan.q: Can a web hosting landing page take orders directly?
faq_plan.a: Yes, once the Order buttons connect to your billing system. The app Emergent builds can connect to any tool with an API, passing the chosen plan and term to checkout and syncing prices back to the cards.

faq_plan.q: How do I add site migration requests to a web hosting landing page?
faq_plan.a: Add a short form that asks which host the site is on now, its address, and its size in GB, and save each request as a row. Set a size limit, such as 10 GB. The app can alert an engineer by Slack or email when a request goes over it.

faq_plan.q: Can I put a domain search on a web hosting landing page?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if your registrar offers an API for availability checks. Connect it, and the page sends the name a visitor types to that API and lists which extensions are open.

faq_plan.q: How is a web hosting landing page different from a home page?
faq_plan.a: A home page serves everyone, from customers logging in to job seekers. A web hosting landing page serves one visitor arriving from an ad or a search, with one job: pick a plan and click Order. Leave off the main navigation that leads anywhere else.

plan.angle: The live SERP for web hosting landing page is design galleries and theme listings (ThemeForest, Behance, Figma) plus posts on where to host a page, and none of them shows what happens after a visitor clicks Order. This page shows four hosting-company pages at work: a shared plan page with the renewal price under every intro price and each order click saved by plan, a free migration form that routes large sites to an engineer, a WordPress plan finder that recommends a plan from two answers, and a VPS region waitlist that counts signups by server size. It makes no uptime or speed claims, and tells hosts to quote an uptime figure only as their service agreement states it.
